executiveSummary: All 10 NVST workflow SKILL.md files have been updated with a '## Reasoning Protocol' section implementing Chain of Draft (CoD) for internal reasoning. FR-1 through FR-5 are fully satisfied: every skill contains the section, all specify ≤ ~5-word draft steps, all distinguish internal vs. user-facing output, and no existing sections were removed or altered. FR-6 (placement 'near the top, before main job steps') is partially satisfied: nine skills place the section immediately after the title, but 'execute-automated-fix' places '## Inputs' before '## Reasoning Protocol', meaning the protocol is not the first major section. A minor wording inconsistency also exists: 'refine-project-context' omits the tilde in '≤ 5 words' vs. '≤ ~5 words' used by most other skills.
minorObservations: In 'execute-automated-fix/SKILL.md', the '## Inputs' section (a reference table) appears at line 13, before '## Reasoning Protocol' at line 23. FR-6 requires the protocol to be placed before the main job steps to be 'loaded into context first'. '## Inputs' is not a job-step section, but it does precede the protocol, partially undermining the FR-6 intent.

In 'refine-project-context/SKILL.md', the step-length instruction reads '≤ 5 words' (no tilde), while all other nine skills use '≤ ~5 words'. This minor wording inconsistency affects FR-4 (consistent pattern across skills).

The 'audit-prototype' and 'refactor-prototype' skills place '## Reasoning Protocol' immediately after the title (lines 11), giving them the best possible placement; this pattern is the recommended standard for all skills.
conclusionsAndRecommendations: The implementation is high-quality and substantially complete. All 10 skills satisfy the core CoD requirements (FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-5) and all 10 user stories comply. Two minor gaps exist: (1) move '## Reasoning Protocol' above '## Inputs' in 'execute-automated-fix/SKILL.md' to fully satisfy FR-6; (2) harmonise the tilde in 'refine-project-context/SKILL.md' from '≤ 5 words' to '≤ ~5 words' to satisfy FR-4. Both fixes are trivial, low-risk changes that can be applied in a focused refactor pass.
